title: ai_request_guard plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_request_guard` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiRequestGuardConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiRequestGuardConfig.description: Plugin: ai_request_guard — Validates and constrains AI/LLM API requests. All five numeric limits (`max_tokens_limit`, `default_max_tokens`, `max_choices`, `max_messages`, `max_prompt_characters`) are unsigned 64-bit integers: negative, fractional, and above-`uint64` values are rejected at plugin construction, and `0` is a valid, maximally strict setting rather than "unset" (omit the field to leave the policy unconfigured). Two relationships between sibling values are also enforced at construction and are **not** expressible in JSON Schema 2020-12, so a schema-valid configuration can still be refused by `ferrum-edge validate` and at startup; operator tooling must apply them as supplemental validation: `default_max_tokens` must be `<=` `max_tokens_limit` when both are set, and `temperature_range[0]` must be `<=` `temperature_range[1]`.

max_tokens_limit.description: Maximum allowed output-token request value across OpenAI and provider-native token fields (including both Gemini ProtoJSON spellings, `generationConfig.maxOutputTokens` and `generation_config.max_output_tokens`). Request caps spelled as integral floats, exponents, or quoted integers are evaluated (and clamped) by value; a present cap that is not a non-negative integer (negative, fractional, boolean, unparseable string, ...) is rejected with HTTP 400 in both reject and clamp modes. Unsigned 64-bit integer; `0` is accepted and refuses any request that asks for a positive number of tokens. When `default_max_tokens` is also set it must not exceed this value — a construction-time relationship JSON Schema cannot express (see the component description).

enforce_max_tokens.description: Reject (400 error) or clamp (silently cap) max_tokens

default_max_tokens.description: Unsigned 64-bit integer (`0` accepted), and must be <= max_tokens_limit when that limit is also configured — a construction-time relationship JSON Schema cannot express (see the component description). Inject a default output-token limit if no supported token field is present (a JSON null cap counts as absent and is replaced); top-level-shaped bodies keep a family-correct top-level fallback (max_output_tokens for Responses, else max_tokens) so a spoofed provider marker or stray cross-provider alias cannot uncap them, while unambiguously provider-native bodies receive only their native cap (including TGI parameters.max_new_tokens). With supported_schema bedrock_converse every body receives inferenceConfig.maxTokens (created when absent) and no top-level cap

max_choices.description: Maximum completions one request may ask for, across OpenAI `n` and `best_of`, Cohere `num_generations`, Gemini `generationConfig.candidateCount` (both ProtoJSON spellings), and TGI `parameters.best_of`. `max_tokens_limit` bounds tokens per completion, so the worst case per request is `max_choices` × `max_tokens_limit`. A larger or non-integer value is rejected with HTTP 400. A request that omits the count (or sends `0`) is counted as the provider default of one completion, so `0` refuses every request. Unsigned 64-bit integer.

supported_schema.description: Request schema family accepted when strict_schema is true. bedrock_converse also binds default_max_tokens injection to Amazon Bedrock Converse (inferenceConfig.maxTokens, created when the optional inferenceConfig is absent)

strict_schema.description: Reject JSON request bodies that do not match supported_schema coverage

allowed_models.description: Whitelist of allowed model names (empty = allow all). Matched against the body model and against any model the request path selects (Gemini/Vertex models/{model}:{method}, Bedrock model/{modelId}/converse|invoke, Azure openai/deployments/{deployment}); every model found must be allowed

blocked_models.description: Blacklist of model names (takes precedence over allowed). Matched against the body model and any request-path model (see allowed_models)

require_model_for_model_policy.description: Require a non-empty string model field when allowed_models or blocked_models is configured, unless the request path selects a model (see allowed_models). Setting false only relaxes a genuinely-absent model; a present-but-invalid model (non-string or empty/whitespace) is still rejected with HTTP 400

require_user_field.description: Require a non-empty string user field in the request body (null and blank values are rejected)

max_messages.description: Maximum message entries across messages, Responses input, Gemini contents, and Cohere chat_history arrays. Unsigned 64-bit integer; `0` is accepted and refuses any request that carries a counted message entry.

max_prompt_characters.description: Maximum total prompt characters (Unicode scalar values; `0` is accepted and refuses any request carrying counted text) across prompt/input/system fields, message text, text multimodal parts, Bedrock Converse messages[].content[].toolResult content and guardContent text, tools (including Bedrock Converse toolConfig.tools[]), tool arguments (including Bedrock Converse messages[].content[].toolUse.input) and Gemini contents[].parts[].functionResponse.response tool results, document/RAG fields (including Anthropic text document source.data and every eligible member value of a Cohere documents[] map, minus its id and _excludes-named members), Google Vertex legacy predict instances[].prompt, and Azure "On Your Data" data_sources[]/dataSources[].parameters.role_information/roleInformation

temperature_range.description: Allowed [min, max] range for top-level temperature plus Gemini generationConfig.temperature / generation_config.temperature and Bedrock inferenceConfig.temperature; conflicting aliases are rejected. Both bounds must be finite and temperature_range[0] must be <= temperature_range[1] — a construction-time relationship JSON Schema cannot express (see the component description)

block_system_prompts.description: Reject system/developer prompt fields and roles, including Responses instructions, provider-native top-level system fields, and Azure "On Your Data" data_sources[]/dataSources[].parameters.role_information/roleInformation (a de-facto system instruction the backend applies)

system_prompt_aliases.description: Additional message roles or top-level fields treated as system prompts when block_system_prompts is true

required_metadata_fields.description: Required top-level fields in the request body; each must be present, not null, and not a blank string

fail_on_uninspectable_body.description: Reject in-scope POST requests whose body cannot be inspected because the buffered body is missing, empty, non-UTF-8, malformed JSON, ambiguous JSON (duplicate object member names, including escaped spellings, or a document over the duplicate-scan budgets), or still compressed after request transforms (no compression/decompress_request decoded it). Set false only for compatibility when the backend must handle such uninspectable bodies itself.
